outcome_intro: Ask your AI "which customer needs attention first?" and get one answer across Firebox, Endpoint Security, ThreatSync and license allocation for every account you manage in WatchGuard Cloud. Each product is a separate WatchGuard API, and Endpoint Security answers for a customer only with a token minted for that customer. This skill mints those tokens for you, fans out across your customers and ranks what needs you.

instead_of_say.instead: Opening each customer in WatchGuard Cloud to check offline Fireboxes, unprotected endpoints, open ThreatSync incidents and expiring licenses, one product view at a time
instead_of_say.say: Which customer needs my attention first?

instead_of_say.instead: Switching into every subscriber account to find computers that are unprotected, out of date, isolated or waiting on a reboot
instead_of_say.say: Which endpoints across my customers are unprotected or out of date?

instead_of_say.instead: Refreshing the deployment status in WatchGuard Cloud after pushing a Firebox configuration change
instead_of_say.say: Tell me when the deployment to FB-12345 finishes, and whether it failed.

pain_points: WatchGuard Endpoint Security answers for a managed customer only with an access token minted for that customer's audience value, which you look up per account first (WatchGuard API docs, Authentication). A device-level question about every customer is a token request and at least one call per customer.

Firebox Management, Endpoint Security, ThreatSync, NDR, AuthPoint and license allocation are separate APIs with their own paths, paging and status codes, so a customer review spans many screens or many scripts even where an API can list every customer at once.

Allocations and the Fireboxes that actually report in drift apart. A WatchGuard Community thread (May 2023, still open in September 2024) shows retired, unallocated Fireboxes staying in the inventory and inflating the device count, with a support case as the only way out.
A Firebox deployment or certificate install is asynchronous: the API hands back a transaction ID and you poll it to learn whether the change landed or failed.

outcomes.question: Which customer needs attention first across Firebox, endpoints, ThreatSync and licenses?
Which endpoints are unprotected, out of date, isolated or waiting on a reboot, across every customer?
Which new ThreatSync incidents from the last 30 days need triage first, and which has nobody touched?
Which customers and computers are exposed to this CVE?
Which Fireboxes and access points went offline, came back or changed firmware since the last sync?
Which Fireboxes are running older firmware than the rest of the same model in my fleet?
Which allocations don't match the Fireboxes that actually report in, and what expires this month?
Did the Firebox deployment finish, or fail?

different_vs_wrappers: The only other MCP server for WatchGuard Cloud we found on GitHub as of October 2026, [WYRE-AI/watchguard-cloud-mcp](https://github.com/WYRE-AI/watchguard-cloud-mcp), covers the platform's account, activation and operator APIs and lists Firebox and Endpoint Security as out of scope for now. This skill covers 208 operations from 13 of WatchGuard's published API specifications (Firebox Management and Reports, FireCloud, Endpoint Security, ThreatSync, NDR assets and Smart Alerts, AuthPoint authentication, and the platform's accounts, operators, activations, license allocation and authorization APIs), mints a separate token for each managed account where WatchGuard requires one, so one Service Provider credential reaches every customer, and keeps a local SQLite mirror so `firebox-devices changes` and `firmware-lag` can compare your fleet over time.
different_vs_vendor: WatchGuard Cloud stays where you configure Fireboxes, policies and endpoint security, and ThreatSync keeps doing its own correlation. This skill complements them by answering cross-customer, cross-product questions from the AI agent you already use, through WatchGuard's public API, in one command.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, so you run the WatchGuard MCP server in its built-in HTTP mode with a bearer token (WATCHGUARD_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN) and put it behind an HTTPS tunnel or reverse proxy. No bridge package is needed. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your credentials once.
Your data stays on your machine. The CLI, MCP server, and the local mirror are all local. The AI sees query results, not raw bulk data, and credentials are never bundled or transmitted by MSP Skills.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

WatchGuard Cloud API access: as an Owner or Administrator, open Administration > Managed Access and click Enable API Access (a Service Provider does this from Subscriber view of its own account). You get a read-write Access ID, a read-only Access ID, the passwords you set for each, and an API key. Set WATCHGUARD_CLIENT_ID to an Access ID, WATCHGUARD_CLIENT_SECRET to its password, WATCHGUARD_API_KEY to the API key and WATCHGUARD_ACCOUNT_ID to your account ID (ACC-... or WGC-...), then run watchguard-cli doctor. For a reporting-only agent, use the read-only Access ID.

faqs.q: Does it work across all my customers, or one account at a time?
faqs.a: Across all of them, with a Service Provider account. accounts health, endpoint-devices posture and endpoint-patches exposure list the accounts you manage, mint a separate token for each one and report every customer in one result, naming any account they could not reach. threatsync-incidents queue reads incidents for all your managed accounts in one ThreatSync call. If any read fails, including a product a customer does not have, these commands exit 6 and say which account and product; accounts health lists that account first with complete: false instead of showing zeros, and an account it could not reach at all appears in fetch_failures. To work on one customer, set WATCHGUARD_AUDIENCE to that customer's audience value (watchguard-cli audiences --account-id <customer-account-id> returns it) and WATCHGUARD_ACCOUNT_ID to that customer's account ID. That is a convenience, not a security boundary: WatchGuard's audience token also works on your own account.

faqs.q: My WatchGuard Cloud account is in Europe or Asia Pacific. Does it work?
faqs.a: Yes. Set WATCHGUARD_BASE_URL and WATCHGUARD_TOKEN_URL to your region's gateway: https://api.deu.cloud.watchguard.com for EMEA or https://api.jpn.cloud.watchguard.com for APAC, with /oauth/token on the end for the token URL. The default is the North America gateway, api.usa.cloud.watchguard.com. Managed Access in WatchGuard Cloud shows your account's API URL as https://api.<region>.cloud.watchguard.com/rest/; drop the /rest/ when you set WATCHGUARD_BASE_URL (the CLI adds it to every path).

faqs.q: Will this hit my WatchGuard API rate limits?
faqs.a: WatchGuard allows 500 requests per second and 200,000 requests per day per API key; a 429 means the day's quota is spent until 00:00 UTC. The cross-customer commands fetch at most four accounts in parallel by default (--concurrency) and stop at --max-pages per account, --rate-limit caps requests per second, GET responses are cached for 5 minutes, and sync keeps a local copy that search, analytics and --data-source local read without calling the API.

faqs.q: Can my AI isolate devices or change firewall policy?
faqs.a: Only if you let it. Write commands such as endpoint-devices isolate, endpoint-devices uninstall, firebox-deployments and the delete commands send as soon as they run; there is no confirmation prompt. Preview any of them with --dry-run first. For a reporting agent, use the read-only Access ID, or set WATCHGUARD_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 so the MCP server drops its write tools and refuses every non-GET call through watchguard_execute.

faqs.q: Has it been tested against a live WatchGuard Cloud account?
faqs.a: Not yet. Every command was built from WatchGuard's published OpenAPI specifications and tested against a local mock of those APIs, not a real account. If you run it against your own WatchGuard Cloud account, tell us what worked or broke on the GitHub issue tracker or at a Build Session; a real MSP run is what earns the live-verified badge.

governance_summary: The skill is read-first: the cross-customer reports, sync, search and nearly every list and get command only read. The exceptions are the reads whose output carries a secret (BOVPN tunnels, Firebox certificates, networks, users, content filtering and the activation keys from activations), which belong with the credential commands; the local mirror and response cache never store those fields. Every write sends immediately with no confirmation prompt, so preview with --dry-run and keep endpoint actions, deployments and deletes human-in-the-loop. The read-only Access ID is the outer limit for a reporting agent.

credentials_note: Credentials stay on your machine, but not only in your environment: the token the CLI mints for your own account is cached in its credentials.toml (mode 0600), and `auth login` given `--client-id` or `--client-secret` also saves that Access ID and password there, so removing the environment variables does not revoke access - run `watchguard-cli auth logout` or disable the Access ID in WatchGuard Cloud. Per-customer tokens stay in memory and are never written to disk
